authorization: Researcher prioritizes decoding phase transitions and correction thresholds in the continuing Lab 008 study.
question: Can a positive-probability critical-crossing event support an injective, charge-preserving odd-parity switching map and thereby lower-bound the physical midpoint Bayes LER directly?
earliest_gate: Define the map on original binary current configurations. It must preserve the full measured charge Q, flip logical parity, preserve midpoint probability, and be injective or have a proved size-independent multiplicity bound.
alternatives: Construct a canonical involution or bounded-multiplicity pairing on an RSW event of size-independent probability, proving a nonzero midpoint LER.
Show that every natural canonical-path switch loses injectivity or event invariance, identifying the exact combinatorial obstruction without inferring correctability.
Reduce the required pairing to a sharper multi-arm or local-gadget probability not supplied by ordinary RSW, preserving it as an explicit theorem prerequisite.
planned_steps: Formulate the paired-mass inequality sum_Q min(N0,N1) >= number of disjoint cross-sector pairs, so the argument targets the physical record average rather than every record.
Test leftmost/rightmost residual-path and local plaquette switches for charge preservation, parity flip, involution/injectivity, and selector stability.
Use only the stored exact L3/L4 current tables to find collisions or verify a bounded finite motif; do not add sizes, samples, decoder runs, or threshold fits.
Connect any surviving event to an RSW or arm-event lower bound only after its hypotheses and boundary geometry are explicit.
stop_rule: Stop at a proved pairing bound, the first exact collision/selector obstruction for each registered natural switch, or an explicit missing percolation event theorem. Do not substitute finite pairing fractions for an asymptotic threshold claim.
outcome: Every simple residual rough-to-rough path flip preserves full charge and flips logical parity. Lower/upper extremal selectors are noninjective on the full crossing event, though their selector-stable subsets form finite involutions. Standalone directed plaquette flips never change logical parity. Ordinary RSW does not lower-bound selector stability, so no asymptotic Bayes lower bound follows.
